CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where should beginners stay in the pool? (1 mark)
   A. Under a diving board
   B. The shallow end
   C. The deep end
   D. Wherever

2. Which is a rule for water games? (1 mark)
   A. Dunk friends
   B. Do not hold anyone under water
   C. Ignore the whistle
   D. Play alone

3. Swimming is important because (1 mark)
   A. it replaces school
   B. it is a life skill that helps keep you safe near water
   C. it makes water disappear
   D. it needs no rules

4. A glide is (1 mark)
   A. moving through water after a push without kicking
   B. a fast kick
   C. a dive
   D. a float on the back

5. In water tag, players (1 mark)
   A. push others
   B. hold others under water
   C. walk fast, not run, and tag gently
   D. run on the pool side

6. You begin a glide by (1 mark)
   A. pushing gently off the wall
   B. jumping from a height
   C. swimming hard
   D. kicking the wall in anger

7. A hare hop suits a rhythm that is (1 mark)
   A. quick like ta-te ta-te
   B. silent
   C. absent
   D. very slow

8. What happens when the hawk tags the last chick? (1 mark)
   A. The hen goes home
   B. The game ends forever
   C. The hawk sleeps
   D. The chick becomes the hawk

9. Why are indigenous games part of our heritage? (1 mark)
   A. They were bought yesterday
   B. They are foreign
   C. They have no meaning
   D. They come to us from earlier generations

10. The giraffe stretch mainly improves (1 mark)
   A. flexibility
   B. smell
   C. hearing
   D. only speed

11. In the hawk and the chicks game, the chicks (1 mark)
   A. sing
   B. hit the hawk
   C. run away
   D. hold on gently behind the hen

12. The elephant walk is done by (1 mark)
   A. jumping high
   B. running
   C. crawling
   D. bending forward and letting your arms hang like a trunk

13. How are indigenous games mostly learnt? (1 mark)
   A. By reading long books only
   B. By watching and joining in
   C. By watching TV only
   D. By buying kits

14. How should you care for displayed works? (1 mark)
   A. Do not touch or write on them
   B. Tear the corners
   C. Leave them in the rain
   D. Touch to feel the paint

15. To analyse a work of art means to (1 mark)
   A. paint over it
   B. ignore it
   C. look closely at its parts to understand it
   D. throw it away

16. Aesthetic refers to (1 mark)
   A. how cheap it is
   B. how beautiful or pleasing something is
   C. how heavy it is
   D. how long it is

17. When the anthem is sung, you should (1 mark)
   A. play
   B. stand straight and be quiet
   C. run
   D. sit and talk

18. A good sportsperson (1 mark)
   A. congratulates winners and encourages losers
   B. quits
   C. argues with the referee
   D. cheats

19. Two stars and a wish means (1 mark)
   A. two lines and a circle
   B. two mistakes and a prize
   C. two good comments and one suggestion
   D. two songs and a wish

20. In a folk song, the chorus (1 mark)
   A. paints
   B. conducts the umpire
   C. hides
   D. answers and repeats

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State four things you would look for when appreciating a sports performance. (4 marks)

22. Why is swimming an essential life skill? (2 marks)

23. Describe the roles of the soloist, the chorus and the instrumentalists in a folk song. (3 marks)

24. Describe the sit-and-slide water entry. (3 marks)

25. Describe how to play an animal game safely and fairly from warm-up to the end. (5 marks)

26. State three qualities of good feedback. (3 marks)

27. State three values taught by the Kenya National Anthem. (3 marks)

28. List the components of a folk song that you can analyse. (4 marks)

29. Describe how to do the elephant walk. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — The shallow end
   Shallow water is safer.

2. B — Do not hold anyone under water
   Safety first.

3. B — it is a life skill that helps keep you safe near water
   Swimming helps prevent drowning.

4. A — moving through water after a push without kicking
   Gliding uses the momentum of the push.

5. C — walk fast, not run, and tag gently
   No pushing.

6. A — pushing gently off the wall
   A gentle push is enough.

7. A — quick like ta-te ta-te
   Hares hop quickly.

8. D — The chick becomes the hawk
   Roles change so everyone plays.

9. D — They come to us from earlier generations
   Heritage is what we inherit.

10. A — flexibility
   Stretching increases flexibility.

11. D — hold on gently behind the hen
   Chicks stay in line.

12. D — bending forward and letting your arms hang like a trunk
   Slow heavy steps with arms as a trunk.

13. B — By watching and joining in
   Elders and children play together.

14. A — Do not touch or write on them
   Care keeps them safe.

15. C — look closely at its parts to understand it
   Analysing means studying the parts.

16. B — how beautiful or pleasing something is
   Aesthetic is about beauty.

17. B — stand straight and be quiet
   Show respect.

18. A — congratulates winners and encourages losers
   Fair play and respect.

19. C — two good comments and one suggestion
   Give two positives and one idea to improve.

20. D — answers and repeats
   The chorus responds to the soloist.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Teamwork, skill, safety and sportsmanship.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps people stay safe near water and prevent drowning, and it keeps the body fit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: The soloist leads, the chorus answers and repeats, the instrumentalists play instruments to keep the beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit on the edge with feet in the water, hands on the edge beside the hips. Turn to face the wall and slide gently into the water holding the edge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Warm up and choose soft clear ground. Explain the rules and roles. Play the game without pushing or pulling. Stop at the whistle and give everyone a turn. Cool down and drink water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kind, honest, specific and helpful. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Unity, peace, justice, hard work, service, patriotism and thankfulness to God. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Community of origin, type or occasion, message, participants and their roles, and instruments.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct components.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bend forward at the waist, clasp hands so that the arms hang like a trunk, and walk slowly with heavy steps, swaying the trunk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
